transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 min
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Hsu (Redwood SE), Jamie Rios (Redwood CSM), Nora Kaplan (Everflow Head of ML), Derek Shaw (Everflow Platform Eng), Priya Menon (Everflow Security), Leo Grant (Everflow PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Align pilot scope, define success, schedule benchmarks, gather compliance docs.

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining, i think we can start, we have about an hour, so we'll walk through pilot runway and confirmation of success criteria. quick intros?
[00:12] Nora Kaplan: hi all, Nora here, i'll be owning ML outcomes and acceptance criteria from Everflow side.
[00:18] Derek Shaw: Derek, platform, i'll handle infra and network setup.
[00:22] Priya Menon: Priya, security and compliance. we'll be looking at KMS, audit logs, scoping data residency.
[00:29] Leo Grant: Leo — product owner for the feature the pilot will enable.
[00:33] Marcus Hsu: Marcus, Redwood SE, i'll run the benchmark and help with deployment patterns.
[00:36] Jamie Rios: Jamie, customer success, i'll help with runbooks and onboarding tasks.
[00:40] Avery Chen: awesome. quick agenda: confirm pilot goals, deployment mode (hosted vs private), runbook & topology for staging, bench windows, and finalize action items.

[02:05] Nora Kaplan: to set expectations — for this pilot we care about two things primarily: latency tail (p95 <= 250ms for short prompts) and generation quality parity with our current hosted provider. also need to validate token cost improvements if we use Redwood batching/caching.
[02:25] Avery Chen: great — latency and quality, and cost. when you say current provider, are you referencing your in-house model or a managed API?
[02:31] Nora Kaplan: currently we're on a mix — a managed API for embeddings and a self-hosted model for specific transforms. the managed API is expensive at scale so we're shopping for better economics.

[03:10] Derek Shaw: we also have strict network egress limits, so if we go hosted we'll need to ensure VPC peering or egress allowances. For Private, we'd prefer a VPC deployment behind our transit gateway.
[03:27] Priya Menon: and from compliance, SOC2 is table stakes; we also need to know about key management — preferably customer-managed KMS or HSM for any sealed data.

[04:12] Marcus Hsu: quick note on topology options: 1) Redwood Hosted API (fastest to pilot) with VPC egress rules; 2) Redwood Dedicated in a shared tenancy with reserved capacity; 3) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) which gives you control over KMS and strict network paths. each has tradeoffs for latency, cost, and setup time.
[04:45] Leo Grant: what’s typical time to get a Private deployment stood up?
[04:50] Marcus Hsu: for a standard VPC Private install with our automation, assuming access and firewall rules are in place, we typically see 4–6 weeks for initial handoff. Hosted can be same-day to days, Dedicated ~2–3 weeks depending on capacity.

[06:05] Nora Kaplan: for the pilot we don't have months, ideally 3 weeks to have something end-to-end. so hosted pilot would fit that timeline, but we still need the KMS requirement. can you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[06:20] Avery Chen: short answer: yes, we have options — hosted with envelope encryption where you bring your keys via KMS, or Private if you need complete on-prem. we’ll capture details in the runbook.

[07:12] Derek Shaw: are there any constraints around KV cache persistence? our workloads sometimes warm caches across sessions. we want to avoid cold-start token costs.
[07:26] Marcus Hsu: we do prefix/KV cache persistence in Dedicated and Private; Hosted has short-lived caching but we can provide request-level advice (consistent prefixes, sticky routing) to get similar benefits during pilot. there's also an option for a cache proxy in your VPC for the hosted lane.

[08:30] Priya Menon: can you explain logging/audit surfaces? we need per-token tracing for a short retention window plus exportable audit logs into our SIEM.
[08:40] Jamie Rios: we surface request-level logs, model version, token counts, and latency traces in the Console; and we can forward logs to a customer S3 or SIEM via a secure integration. retention and redaction rules are configurable.

[09:55] Nora Kaplan: quality validation — we have a set of 1500 prompts used for regression tests. we'll attach the corpus after anonymization. what's the best way to run evals?
[10:06] Marcus Hsu: ideal is to run the corpus against the model in staging with deterministic seeds, collect outputs, and run your eval scripts. Redwood supports batch eval runs and we can save outputs to S3 for diffing. Marcus: i'll prep a script that runs in our benchmark container.

[11:20] Derek Shaw: side note: our traffic has spikes tied to business hours, 80% within a 10-hour window. throughput and autoscale behavior matters.
[11:30] Avery Chen: noted. pilot should include a scaled load window to validate autoscaling and cold-starts.

[12:42] Leo Grant: success criteria — Nora mentioned p95 latency and quality parity. can we add availability target for the pilot (like 99.5%) and a cost delta target (e.g., 30% reduction in per-token costs)?
[12:56] Nora Kaplan: yes, let's make those explicit — availability and cost targets are important.

[14:10] Marcus Hsu: okay i'll propose a scoring rubric in the runbook: latency p50/p95, generation quality pass rate on the 1500 prompt set, per-token cost estimate, and operational metrics (autoscale, error rate).

[15:20] Priya Menon: about data residency — some payloads include EU-only PII; we need to ensure routing and storage complies. if we use hosted, can you pin region and ensure EU-only routing?
[15:34] Avery Chen: yes — region pinning exists, and we can provision model serving in a European region and ensure logs/storage remain in-region. we'll include the data flow diagram in the runbook.

[16:50] Derek Shaw: what's the recommended approach for API keys and secrets? we want RBAC for multiple service accounts and auditability.
[16:58] Marcus Hsu: Redwood supports token scopes and RBAC in the Console; for private deployments you can integrate with your SSO and provenance logging. For hosted, we recommend short-lived service tokens and a secrets manager in your VPC, or use our token rotation APIs.

[18:10] Jamie Rios: i'm going to put together the onboarding checklist: access & SSO, network allowlists, sample prompts, evaluation suite, benchmark windows, and production kickoff criteria. we'll share as a living doc.

[19:05] Nora Kaplan: about benchmarks — what's the expected token throughput for your standard mpt64/llama variants? i'm trying to estimate resource needs vs cost.
[19:18] Marcus Hsu: it varies; i'll send a table, but rough numbers: small open models ~50-120 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length; quantized variants and batching affect that a lot. for pilot we'll simulate your actual prompt lengths.

[20:37] Derek Shaw: can the pilot be instrumented to measure per-route cost? we have different product flows and want to attribute costs.
[20:45] Avery Chen: yes, per-route and per-token attribution is in Console; we'll tag routes and give you per-route cost breakdowns during the pilot.

[22:00] Leo Grant: integrations — we use SQS + Lambda to fan requests. does Redwood have recommended adapters for queue-based patterns?
[22:10] Marcus Hsu: yes, we have lightweight SDK patterns for async queue processing, plus a helper that batches requests from a queue to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency. we'll share a sample repo link.

[24:05] Priya Menon: encryption at rest — you said KMS. If we bring our KMS, are model weights encrypted under our key or just the customer payloads?
[24:18] Avery Chen: typically customer payloads, logs, and any customer-managed artifacts are encrypted with customer KMS. Model weights for curated open models are handled by Redwood, but for Private/On-prem we can support additional controls around full-disk encryption and HSM for keys.

[26:40] Nora Kaplan: okay for scheduling — can we aim for a benchmark window the week of May 24th? that gives Derek time to get network rules in place.
[26:52] Derek Shaw: yes that works but need the runbook details to provision the right CIDR ranges.

[27:15] Avery Chen: action: we'll send full runbook and the staging topology by Friday (May 14). that'll include CIDRs, ports, and KMS integration steps.

[29:01] Marcus Hsu: small perceptual note — when you run the 1500 prompts, try to flag prompts that are latency-sensitive vs batch-tolerant; we can tune batching for the latter.

[30:30] Leo Grant: what's our rollback/runaway strategy if the pilot causes errors in production traffic?
[30:39] Avery Chen: we'll recommend a canary routing setup and automatic fallback to your prior provider on a per-route basis — Redwood Console handles canary weight and automatic failover if error thresholds hit.

[32:03] Priya Menon: do you retain full verbatim payloads in logs? our policy is minimal retention and redaction for PII.
[32:13] Jamie Rios: retention & redaction rules are configurable; for pilot we'll advise a minimum retention window and show how to apply automatic redaction filters.

[34:00] Nora Kaplan: on the economics side, is there a clear difference in unit cost between Dedicated and Private?
[34:10] Marcus Hsu: Dedicated gives predictable committed discount on capacity; Private has higher setup overhead but can be cheaper at scale depending on your infra discounts and utilization. We'll run cost models during the pilot.

[36:24] Derek Shaw: network egress charges concern us if we use hosted. can you provide estimates or configurations to minimize egress?
[36:34] Avery Chen: yes, region pinning and VPC peering reduce egress. we'll include sample cost estimates in the runbook.

[38:05] Leo Grant: any gotchas we should know about for Canary deployments?
[38:12] Marcus Hsu: watch for sticky sessions and token-count imbalance — small differences in response length between providers can skew token billing. We'll provide instrumentation to measure and normalize.

[40:00] Nora Kaplan: ok let's lock success criteria: p95 <= 250ms for short prompts, quality parity >= 92% pass rate on the 1500 prompt set, availability >= 99.5% over the benchmark window, and at least 25% reduction in estimated per-token cost vs current provider. agreed?
[40:18] Derek Shaw: agreed from platform.
[40:20] Priya Menon: security team signoff pending documented KMS and audit flows but agreed to criteria subject to that.

[42:00] Jamie Rios: i'll circulate the runbook and rubric after the call.

[43:45] Marcus Hsu: scheduling benchmark — Marcus: propose Wed 2027-05-26 09:00-12:00 UTC for a load window; please confirm availability.
[43:56] Derek Shaw: tentative yes — will confirm by Friday.

[45:05] Nora Kaplan: slight transcription hiccup: we also want to test a fine-tuned variant that we plan to bring later in pilot; is that supported?
[45:18] Marcus Hsu: yes, you can upload models to Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we'll support model artifacts via private model registry with proper RBAC. We'll outline that in the runbook.

[47:40] Derek Shaw: about metrics retention — if we forward to our SIEM, is there a way to get aggregated metrics too?
[47:50] Avery Chen: yes, aggregated metrics in Console and raw logs export; both can be forwarded.

[49:00] Leo Grant: what do you need from Everflow to kick off the runbook work?
[49:08] Avery Chen: primarily: 1) anonymized prompt corpus; 2) traffic histogram; 3) CIDR ranges & network owner contact; 4) compliance checklist items. Derek & Priya will own those.

[50:10] Derek Shaw: we'll start pulling that together. expectation: send prompts and histogram by Wed 2027-05-13.
[50:20] Priya Menon: security will review SOC2 + KMS notes and come back with a short list by 2027-05-17.

[52:05] Jamie Rios: other logistics — we'll create a shared folder and a staging runbook doc. I'll invite everyone and assign owners.

[53:18] Avery Chen: quick reminder — Marcus will run the benchmark scripts and we may ask to run a second window if initial numbers vary. also we'll include per-route cost telemetry.

[55:02] Nora Kaplan: thanks all, this feels good. two small concerns: 1) need clarity on KMS for hosted lane; 2) ensure we can run the eval scripts deterministically.
[55:18] Marcus Hsu: we'll provide deterministic seed options and the KMS design note in the runbook.

[56:20] Avery Chen: recap of next steps: Redwood sends runbook + staging topology by 2027-05-14 (Avery/Jamie); Everflow shares prompt corpus + traffic histogram by 2027-05-13 (Derek); Redwood sets up benchmark scripts and proposes window (Marcus) for 2027-05-26; Priya to send compliance Qs by 2027-05-17.
[56:50] Leo Grant: i'll join the benchmark and keep product-side notes.
[57:05] Nora Kaplan: thanks everyone.
[57:10] Avery Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the shared doc and send calendar invites for the bench window.
[57:20] (meeting ends)

References mentioned: pilot_runbook_draft (link placeholder), benchmark-scripts repo (link placeholder), console-dashboard-example (link placeholder).

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions were left to preserve authenticity (e.g., model names and acronyms).
